indicators: Release ships a .ci-*.sh script and a postinstall hook that dumps CI secrets and runner memory
Part of the WFX Phantom campaign, which also injected workflows into GitHub repositories and reverted the commits within minutes
Packagist flags 3.14.2 (Packagist), 3.14.3 and 3.14.4 (Aikido) as malware and has deleted them; 3.14.1 is the last release before them
summary: Releases 3.14.2, 3.14.3 and 3.14.4 of digitalelvis/neuronai-studio on Packagist carry a CI secret stealer from the WFX Phantom campaign. Packagist flagged them as malware and deleted them.
remediation: Make sure no composer.lock resolves digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.2, 3.14.3 or 3.14.4; go back to 3.14.1. If one of them ran in CI, rotate the secrets and cloud credentials available to that pipeline and review recent workflow runs and commits.

review.notes: Approved by the PO on 2026-11-26 on engineering's recommendation. Second source: Packagist's malware filter (PKFE-x1zg-yk22-m1zr, PKFE-3j6h-zc7y-12gd, PKFE-258q-94rn-mqr6). The draft's remediation (back to 3.14.2) was wrong: 3.14.2 is flagged too. OSV had no record on 2026-11-26.
